title: ～ばかりでなく — not only ～ but also ～
summary: Adds a second item to a first one: “not only ～ but also ～.” It attaches to the plain form of verbs and adjectives, to nouns directly, and to な-adjectives with な. The second half usually has も.

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ ばかりでなく、～も
patterns.gloss: noun + ばかりでなく、～も: 英語ばかりでなく、中国語も

patterns.form: 普通形（な形容詞は〜な） ＋ ばかりでなく、～も
patterns.gloss: 上手なばかりでなく、～も

body.p: The first half names something obvious or basic, and the second half adds something more. 英語ばかりでなく中国語も話せる says he speaks Chinese as well as English. The second half usually has も or まで.
ばかりでなく and だけでなく mean almost the same, but ばかりでなく is a little more formal and written. Both are followed by a positive addition. Negative sentences are possible too: 値段ばかりでなく質もよくない.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は英語（えいご）ばかりでなく、中国語（ちゅうごくご）も話（はな）せます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo bakari de naku, chūgokugo mo hanasemasu.
examples.tr: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

examples.ja: この店（みせ）は料理（りょうり）ばかりでなく、店員（てんいん）の態度（たいど）もいい。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa ryōri bakari de naku, tenin no taido mo ii.
examples.tr: This restaurant has not only good food but also polite staff.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）は歌（うた）が上手（じょうず）なばかりでなく、踊（おど）りも上手（じょうず）だ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa uta ga jōzu na bakari de naku, odori mo jōzu da.
examples.tr: She is not only good at singing but also good at dancing.

pitfalls: な-adjectives need な: 上手なばかりでなく. Nouns attach directly.
Do not forget も (or まで) in the second half; the pair is what gives the “also” meaning.
